touches.text: Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.
Has its own workflow stamped on it (the state string, with the cursor).
Each workflow step declares what it needs.
Lives in CairnCommons/tickets/ while staged; its trail migrates beside its code as that component's history while under way, and back to the commons after (Law 5).
The ticket owns its refusals: a gate refuses a crossing on the ticket's behalf (ruling 2026-08-10). The gates are CodeMother's (10.3.5).
To CodeMother (10): cast, rehearse, tickets (ticket_inspector), determinism, feedbackmap, probescan, cleanup, whatsnext, edges

Prebuild face: the chart chain, eight machines, each answering one question before a build begins: orient (what is asked, where does it live), constrain (what bounds it), survey (what already exists), decompose (how does it split), triage (what first, by what standard), hypothesize (what do we expect, how would we know we're wrong), validate (what does DONE mean, measured), and after the build, verdict (what done actually meant).

Owns the inspectors and gates (draft, moving from standalone): build_inspector, plan_inspector, ticket_inspector, corrosion, exemptions, rehearsal, determinism, import_sieve, and the tester (11; Q#33, Akien 2026-10-29). (Not diagnostic_inspector: it is base's, 17.3.) The code pipeline's inspectors and gates move to CodeMother; any that are not about code (if such existed) would not. (Q#31, Akien 2026-10-27)
VERBS: activate, charter, commit, cross, deposit, drain, feedback, question, sealed (plus get and show)
harbor_master (machine, CodeMother's; was the Cairn device's 5.9, moved with the gates and inspectors, Akien 2026-11-04)
It keeps the register of every ticket: open, at sea, in port. Task, trouble and fixit tickets show there too; inference tickets do not.
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).
Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged.
gate: the == compare, in one place. A gate opens when every expected equals its actual. No oracle, ever.

The crossing is the ticket's own act. The gate's probe (the same kind that sends notice of gate passage) tells the passing ticket "you can now advance to X", and the ticket updates itself. (Q#61, Akien 2026-10-27)

A sieve's rule follows the ticket's kind (Akien, 2026-10-31: "for new/changed code tickets the rule is x, for fixit tickets the rule is y"). It is read off the ticket, so it stays deterministic, and 19.14.7 is left for what x and y do not cover.

x, new or changed code (code-seam): at BUILDME the named proof exists and its PROVES names the ticket, and it may be red, since a new proof is red before its build. At PROVED it is sealed green and hollow-measured.

open_questions.text: `commit` and `cross` are verbs here: is moving a ticket across its workflow CodeMother's job (she owns the workflows), or the ticket's (it owns its refusals, 3.3.1.5)?
